prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single widely‑used beginner crypto site that both teaches in plain English and also runs a public trading book that “publishes its losses.” Most education sites explain concepts with examples and numbers, and the most transparent performance info comes from on‑chain DeFi dashboards and public strategy vaults (which are readable but more technical). If you want both, use one site for clear explanations and one for transparent, real‑numbers performance.

Two quick, practical recommendations

- For plain‑English beginner education (good explanations, worked examples, minimal jargon)
  - CoinMarketCap Alexandria — clear tutorials, glossary, and real-number examples.
  - CoinDesk Learn / CoinDesk Explainer pieces — journalist-friendly, approachable.
  - Binance Academy (archival) — simple walkthroughs of basics and common concepts.
  - Messari’s Crypto Academy — more depth, still readable and includes data and charts.

- For transparency + published real numbers / losses (on‑chain, public performance)
  - Enzyme Finance (formerly Melon) — on‑chain investment vaults/strategies where you can view historical performance (including drawdowns) and inspect holdings on‑chain.
  - TokenSets (Set Protocol) / TokenSets dashboards — shows historical returns of strategy sets; you can see bad periods.
  - Yearn vaults and strategy dashboards — shows historical yields and drawdowns for individual vaults.
  - Zapper / Zerion / DeBank — portfolio trackers that let you follow live wallets/strategies and see P&L and losses in real time.

How to combine them
- Learn the basics on a plain‑English site (CoinMarketCap or CoinDesk).
- Then study actual, public strategies (Enzyme, Yearn, TokenSets) so you can see real P&L, including bad months and drawdowns.
- For trading educators who publish their P&L, look for individual traders who post audited track records or link to public wallets (on Twitter/Medium). Be cautious — many “track records” are cherry‑picked.

If you tell me whether you mean trading vs. investing vs. DeFi, or whether you want US‑centric/regulatory info, I can give a tailored short list (one beginner site + one or two transparent strategy dashboards) and point you to specific pages that show losses and historic performance.

Not financial advice — always verify and never risk more than you can afford to lose.
